verses.1: The apostles and the brothers who lived among the Jews also heard that other nations also accepted the word of God.
verses.2: But when Peter went up to Jerusalem, those who were from the circumcision community testified against him.
verses.3: Saying that you came before men who had swollen testicles, and ate with them.
verses.4: Starting from this point, Peter began to speak to them one by one.
verses.5: I was in the city of Ioppias, praying. In my vision, I saw a huge object descending from heaven. It resembled a large platform with four legs. It came down towards me.
verses.6: To that place where we saw the four corners of the earth, as well as the animals, birds, and other creatures in the sky.
verses.7: I also heard a voice saying to me: “Anastasius, Peter, eat and satisfy your hunger.”
verses.8: I said, “Never, sir! It never entered my mouth, either in a pure or impure manner.”
verses.9: Then a voice was heard from the second heaven. “God has purified you, so that you may not be a scoundrel.”
verses.10: This happened three times, and once again, everything collapsed back into the sky.
verses.11: And I saw three men who threw themselves onto the house during our stay there. They were sent from Caesarea to me.
verses.12: He said that his spirit would go with them, without any difference at all. We went along with him, along with those six brothers. Then we entered the man’s house.
verses.13: He also told us how he saw the angel standing in his house, and that he said, “Send Apostel to Joppa, and send Simon, the man called Peter, there.”
verses.14: Whoever speaks words to you, so that you may be saved, and so that your whole household will also be saved.
verses.15: And as I began to speak, the holy spirit fell upon them, just as it fell upon us at the beginning.
verses.16: I remembered the name of the Lord: John baptised with water, but you shall be baptized in the Holy Spirit.
verses.17: If then God has given them the same gift as we have received from Him, by believing in the Lord Jesus Christ, then who am I to doubt God’s power?
verses.18: When they heard this, they were silent and praised the God. They said, “So also, to all nations, God has given the opportunity to live a life of righteousness.”
verses.19: Those who were scattered from the sorrow that befell Stephen, went as far as Phoenicia, Cyprus, and Antioch. They did not speak their words only to the Jews.
verses.20: Some of them were Cypriots and Cilicians. They went to Antioch and preached to the Hellenists, announcing the good news of Jesus Christ.
verses.21: And when the Lord was with them, a large number of believers returned to the Lord.
verses.22: He heard the words from the church in Jerusalem regarding them. So he sent Barnabas to Antioch.
verses.23: He, who became and saw the grace of God, praised and called upon all to follow the example of his heart, to serve the Lord.
verses.24: Because he was a good man, full of holy spirit and faith. And the crowd was ready to serve him.
verses.25: And he went to Tarsus in search of Saul.
verses.26: And after finding him, he brought him to Antioch. It happened that during those years, he spent all his time teaching the people in the church. He also managed to get financial support for his work among the Christian students in Antioch.
verses.27: On those days, a prophet came from Jerusalem to Antioch.
verses.28: One of them was named Hagabos. He predicted that a great famine would occur throughout the entire region due to the spirit’s influence. This happened in the land of Claudius.
verses.29: And as the teacher saw fit, he assigned each of his disciples to serve among the Jewish brothers who lived there.
verses.30: And they also sent them out, through the hands of Barnabas and Saul, to the elders.
